items.title: Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World
items.summary: If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant. items.title: Rasen, out in early access now, is a PvP focused take on Dark Souls that borrows one of fighting games' best techy tricks
items.summary: The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring , I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access. items.title: Casualties: Unknown Is A Brutal 97%-Rated Survival Game That Will Make You Realize Your Mortality, And At A Cheap Price, Too
items.summary: There’s no light. The shuttle that brought me into the depths is fitted with just a shower, and the darkness swallows everything around me. Each step is as painful as the last, like walking barefoot on LEGO bricks, as I narrowly miss traps. Corpses are frozen as I head further down, a reminder of who came before and likely what I’ll end up as. I crack the glass of a small base, crawling through to gain access, shrapnel filling my foot as I sneak through. Infection rises, but with no medicine, it spreads. It gets worse. It gets worse.
